step1_analysis.description: A compact linear circuit model for a standing-wave oscillator. It consists of a lossy transmission line segment (modeled as R, L, C) and a negative conductance (modeled as R2) to compensate for losses and sustain oscillation.

paper_reference.title: A 10-GHz Global Clock Distribution Using Coupled Standing-Wave Oscillators

oscillation_frequency.description: The steady-state oscillation frequency of the standing-wave oscillator.

sky130_expected.calculation: Determined by the LC tank resonance: f = 1 / (2 * pi * sqrt(L * C)). For L=0.5nH and C=0.5pF, f is approximately 10 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The frequency is primarily set by the passive LC components, which can be tuned to match the paper's 10 GHz target.

resonant_peak_magnitude.description: The peak magnitude of the AC response at the resonant frequency.

sky130_expected.calculation: Depends on the net parallel resistance of the tank (Rp || Rneg).
sky130_expected.reasoning: A high peak indicates the negative resistance is effectively canceling the tank losses, approaching the oscillation condition.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure the oscillation frequency and AC resonant peak of the standing-wave oscillator model.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Standing-Wave Oscillator Model Testbench

.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param R_val=5
.param L_val=0.5n
.param C_val=0.5p
.param Rneg_val=-150

* DUT
R IN N1 {R_val}
L N1 OUT {L_val}
C OUT GND {C_val}
R2 OUT GND {Rneg_val}

* Ground definition
VGND GND 0 DC 0

* Stimulus
VIN IN 0 DC 0 AC 1 PULSE(0 1 0 1p 1p 10p 100p)

.control
  * AC Analysis
  ac dec 100 1G 100G
  let vout_mag = vdb(OUT)
  meas ac peak_mag max vout_mag
  
  * Transient Analysis
  tran 1p 2n
  meas tran t1 trig v(OUT) val=0 rise=10
  meas tran t2 trig v(OUT) val=0 rise=11
  let osc_period = t2 - t1
  let osc_freq = 1 / osc_period
  
  print osc_freq
  print peak_mag
  quit
.endc
.end
